transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

OE is a drain error. The machine can't pump the water out. Here's what you can try, roughly from easiest to most involved.

## 1. Quick checks (no water involved)
• Restart it. Switch off at the wall for a minute, switch back on, and select Spin Only (or Rinse+Spin). Sometimes it's a one-off glitch.
• Check the drain hose (the grey hose at the back). Pull the machine out a little and make sure it isn't kinked, squashed against the wall, or pushed too far down the standpipe. It should go no more than about 15 cm into the pipe.
• Check where it drains to. In UK kitchens the hose often connects to the spigot under the sink. If that sink trap or spigot is clogged with lint or food, the washer can't drain. Disconnect the hose there, clear any gunk, and check the spigot isn't blocked. If the sink plumbing was recently changed, a blanking cap left inside the new spigot is a classic cause.
• Cold weather: if the machine is in a garage or outbuilding, the hose may have frozen.

Then try Spin Only again.

## 2. Drain it by gravity, avoiding the front door
Unhook the main drain hose from the sink or standpipe and lower the end into a bucket on the floor, below the level of the water in the drum. Water will often siphon or trickle out this way. Lift the hose up to stop the flow while you empty the bucket. It's slow, but it keeps the water away from the kitchen floor.

## 3. Use the small emergency hose behind the flap
Behind that bottom-right flap on your LG there's usually a small thin drain tube next to the big round filter cap. This is what prevents the flood:
• Put down towels and use a shallow tray (a baking tray or roasting tin works better than a bucket, because it fits under the machine).
• Pull out the small tube, remove its plug, and let it drain into the tray. Plug it back in when the tray is nearly full, empty it, and repeat. A full drum can be 10 to 20 litres, so expect several rounds.
• Only once that's run dry, unscrew the big filter cap. It will usually have a sock, coin, hair grip, or lint wedged in it, which is the most common cause of OE.

The flood last time almost certainly happened because the big filter cap was opened with the drum still full. Draining through the small tube first avoids that.

## If none of that works
If the hose and sink are clear and the filter is clean but it still shows OE, the drain pump has probably failed. That's a call for LG service or an engineer.

Let me know what you find and I can help narrow it down.

I've pulled the machine out and the hose was squashed behind it, so I've straightened it. Spin again and it drains a bit slower than normal then goes back to OE. I'm still not unscrewing that filter myself.

Good find. Draining slower than normal and then OE again suggests there's still a partial blockage somewhere. It's in one of three places: the hose, the sink plumbing, or the filter/pump. You can narrow it down without touching the filter.

## Test: is it the sink side or the machine side?
1. Unhook the drain hose from the sink spigot or standpipe.
2. Put the end in a bucket on the floor (hold it up until you're ready so water doesn't siphon out).
3. Run Spin Only with the hose in the bucket.

If it drains quickly and finishes without OE, the problem is your sink plumbing, not the washer.
• Clear the spigot (the stub the hose pushes onto) with a screwdriver or bottle brush. Lint builds up there.
• Unscrew the sink trap (the U-bend under the sink) with a bowl underneath and clear any gunk.
• Reconnect and test again.

If it's still slow into the bucket, the blockage is in the machine. Common culprits are coins, hair grips, tissues, or a sock in the filter or pump.

## Also check the hose itself
Since it was squashed, run your hand along its full length. If it has a permanent flattened crease, it may still be restricting flow even when straightened. Replacement drain hoses are cheap and easy to fit.

## Getting your clothes out
The door stays locked while there's water in the drum. Use the bucket method above: lower the hose into a bucket on the floor and let it drain by gravity, lifting the hose to pause while you empty it. Once the water's low, the door should unlock after a minute or two. If it doesn't, switch the machine off at the wall and wait a couple of minutes.

Try not to keep re-running spin cycles in the meantime, as the pump can overheat struggling against a blockage.

## If it's the machine side
Book a repair. LG's UK service line or any local washing machine engineer can do it, and a filter/pump clear is usually a quick, routine job. It's worth mentioning "OE error, drains slowly" when you call so they come prepared.
The kitchen sink drains fine, no problems there. I'm nervous about unhooking the hose over my laminate though. If it's not the sink side, what do you think it is?

## The sink draining fine doesn't fully rule out the sink side

The washer hose usually connects to a separate spigot on the waste pipe, below the sink bowl. That small stub can clog with lint even while the sink itself drains normally. If your hose goes into a standpipe instead, that standpipe can block independently too. So it's still worth a look if you're willing.

## If it's the machine, the likely causes (most to least common)

1. Blocked drain filter. By far the most common cause. Coins, hair grips, bra wires, tissues and lint collect there. Slow draining followed by OE is the classic symptom.
2. Debris in the pump impeller. Something small gets past the filter and jams or slows the pump. You might hear the pump humming, buzzing or rattling during spin.
3. Damaged drain hose. It was squashed, so it may have a permanent crease or kink that still restricts flow even when straightened.
4. Weak or failing drain pump. Less likely if it was fine until recently, but possible if it's been struggling against a blockage for a while.
5. Blocked sump hose. This is the internal hose between drum and pump. A sock can get lodged here. It's an engineer job.

My honest guess is #1, with #3 as a close second given what you found.

## Protecting the laminate if you do the bucket test
• Lay old towels down first, with a bin bag under them if you have one.
• Use a bucket that's lower than the machine. Keep the hose end held up high until it's inside the bucket, then lower it. Raise it again to stop the flow.
• Stay with it the whole time, and stop before the bucket is more than half full so it's easy to carry.
• Any spill wiped up within a few minutes won't harm laminate. It's standing water that does damage.

## If you'd rather not touch it at all
That's completely reasonable. Leave it switched off and book an engineer. Say "LG F4V5VYP0W, OE error, drains slowly, hose was kinked and has been straightened." A filter or pump clear is a quick, routine job, and they'll drain it safely.

Avoid running more spin cycles while you wait, so the pump doesn't overheat.
